answer: eFuse die identity gates admission: a foundry burns a one-time fuse pattern into each chip, signed by the fab's private root key. Verification reads the fuse map, checks the signature, grants one identity per die. Forging N identities needs N physical dies; a wafer tapeout costs eighty thousand dollars in masks. A farm cannot share fuses or rewrite a burned pattern: eFuses are atomic, so bulk buys silicon, not accounts. Clusters get their fab lot blacklisted and dies revoked. Like one plume over a grove, a fuse stays burned, and the orchard of fakes withers from one scorched row.
